proposed_from.topic: Revive parent exp_platform_ncc_drift_minimax_frontier with a phase-correct all-kernel comparison rather than its refuted all-positive-floor claim. In the unchanged bounded finite-population adaptive platform model, prove that the optimized clipped predictable-AIPW radius R* and unrestricted uniformly honest variable-length minimax expected length L* are uniformly comparable iff the common available-arm floor p_floor exceeds alpha. For p_floor>alpha, establish M(p_floor-alpha)s <= L* <= 2R* <= [8 sqrt((1-p_floor)/(alpha p_floor))/(p_floor-alpha)]L*, s^2=sum_{b in W}q_b^2/n_b, under arbitrary outcome-adaptive propensities. For p_floor<=alpha, prove no finite uniform comparison and solve the one-window-unit boundary exactly. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A product-uniform prior on focal potential outcomes with all controls zero stays in every TV budget pathwise. Conditional on the actual adaptive record, unseen focal coordinates remain independent uniforms. A weighted-uniform density lemma and missing squared-weight mass Q yield E(Qc)>=(p_floor-alpha)s^2 and hence L*>=M(p_floor-alpha)s. Concurrent weights give the displayed upper constant. The continuous one-unit experiment has L*=2M[p_floor-alpha]_+ and R*=2M above the boundary, proving sharp 1/(p_floor-alpha) blow-up. In the nonadaptive one-unit three-block family, L*=(1-alpha)D+(2M-D)[p_floor-alpha]_+, D=min(Gamma,2M), so strict all-kernel NCC gain holds iff Gamma<2M. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently audit the posterior factorization, density lemma, and inherited radius constants; obtain an intrinsic strict-NCC-gain criterion for general continuous outcome-adaptive designs or state its impossibility boundary without substituting an AIPW KKT result. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the one-unit continuum proof, then condition the product prior through an outcome-adaptive two-unit assignment tree and verify that no missing focal coordinate enters the record likelihood; any failure, or any compatible design violating the Q coverage-budget inequality, kills the positive theorem. seed_details.anchor_locator: Open-ended Question on the fixed common propensity floor and the terminal review directive.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize \(p_{\mathrm{floor}}>\alpha\) as necessary and sufficient for a finite uniform comparison between the optimized clipped predictable-AIPW radius and unrestricted honest minimax expected length, and derive the sharp blow-up order at the boundary.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the parent's separated two-prior modulus by a product-uniform prior and a posterior missing-squared-weight-mass inequality under the actual adaptive record.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining adaptive experiments, propensity floors, confidence-interval expected length, and minimaxity returned adaptive Wald, conditional Gaussian, and fixed-experiment minimax papers, but no coverage-level floor phase theorem.
seed_details.red_team: The result is immediate from the parent's fixed-floor open question once positivity is imposed.
seed_details.rebuttal: Positivity alone was the parent's unresolved gap; the new step is an all-kernel Bayes lower bound that survives arbitrary outcome feedback and identifies the exact \(p_{\mathrm{floor}}-\alpha\) coverage budget.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Proposition on computability via the adaptive-record factorization and Section on discussion and outlook.
seed_details.kernel: Give a filtration-level necessary and sufficient measurability condition under which every unrevealed potential-outcome coordinate retains its product prior after conditioning on an outcome-adaptive record, then convert it into a sharp weighted-missing-mass coverage inequality.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace selective conditioning on a design statistic by disintegration of a least-favorable product prior over fixed schedules along every realized assignment path.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found selective randomization factorization and adaptive finite-population martingale theory, but no posterior-product theorem used for unrestricted confidence-length lower bounds.
seed_details.red_team: This is only the elementary principle that unobserved independent variables remain independent.
seed_details.rebuttal: Outcome-dependent assignment makes the record likelihood schedule dependent; the theorem must show pathwise that every factor is measurable with respect to revealed coordinates and must identify the exact failure condition.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Theorem 3 on efficient influence functions, the deterministic-availability equality discussion, and the Conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize strict nonconcurrent-control gain for unrestricted honest interval kernels by an intrinsic comparison of the full and concurrent observed-data experiments, with necessity and sufficiency under outcome-adaptive propensity metadata.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace equality of two efficient influence functions by a comparison of the coverage-risk sets induced by the two observation maps.
seed_details.destination_search: Adjacent searches found semiparametric NCC efficiency, bounded-bias auxiliary-data minimax intervals, and Bayes--minimax confidence-set duality, but no all-kernel strict-gain criterion for adaptive platform records.
seed_details.red_team: Blackwell comparison makes the answer tautological and yields no usable criterion.
seed_details.rebuttal: The required result must reduce the comparison to a primitive observed-law or coverage-polytope condition and must account for propensity metadata that can encode omitted controls.

seed_details.anchor_locator: The honest-scope clause that fixes the drift budget and the reviewer strengthening path on unknown drift.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the between-drift-class modulus and the sharp price of honest adaptation to an unknown total-variation budget, including discontinuity at \(p_{\mathrm{floor}}=\alpha\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed-budget bias optimizer by a nested-class testing problem and compute the between-class modulus under the adaptive randomization law.
seed_details.destination_search: Cai--Low and Chen--Zhang--Ye provide the fixed Gaussian adaptation template; no adaptive finite-population NCC analogue was located.
seed_details.red_team: The impossibility follows directly from generic nonparametric confidence-interval adaptation theory.
seed_details.rebuttal: The adaptive record law and the coverage-level positivity phase change the between-class geometry, so the Gaussian result does not transfer by model inclusion.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction on welfare-oriented adaptive allocation and Discussion question on confidence-interval optimality.
seed_details.kernel: Choose an adaptive platform design that optimizes welfare regret subject to an all-kernel expected-length competitiveness constraint, and certify the optimal exploration floor.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Promote the predictable propensity sequence from a given design to the decision variable and combine a regret lower bound with the phase constraint \(p_{\mathrm{floor}}>\alpha\).
seed_details.destination_search: The design search found Neyman-regret and adaptive treatment-choice optimality papers, but none with unrestricted confidence-length competitiveness as the inference constraint.
seed_details.red_team: A fixed exploration floor trivially enforces inference and standard bandit analysis supplies regret.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial object is the certified Pareto frontier and the optimal distance above \(\alpha\), not feasibility of a hand-chosen floor.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Theorem on adaptively weighted normal inference and Discussion question on optimal width.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the observed-design information threshold at which optimal conditional adaptive intervals and unrestricted unconditionally honest intervals have comparable expected length.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace martingale studentization by a two-experiment comparison between conditioning on the realized design and averaging over it.
seed_details.destination_search: Chen--Andrews characterizes optimal conditional Gaussian inference, but does not compare it with the unrestricted finite-population minimax expected-length value under bounded outcomes.
seed_details.red_team: Conditional intervals are necessarily longer, so the ordering is immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Ordering does not determine a quantitative equivalence frontier, and conditioning can disclose different information under outcome-adaptive designs.

seed_details.anchor_locator: The three-block kill-test construction and the reviewer objection to an AIPW-only strict-gain claim.
seed_details.kernel: Solve the continuous one-window-unit minimax interval problem for every drift budget and characterize strict all-kernel NCC gain by \(\Gamma<2M\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a finite-grid randomized-interval linear program by Tonelli integration over a continuum prior and a two-branch coverage-allocation program.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact continuum confidence-allocation calculation was not found in platform-trial or bounded-bias auxiliary-data papers.
seed_details.red_team: A one-unit experiment is a toy calculation with no general content.
seed_details.rebuttal: It supplies the exact boundary witness, proves the necessary blow-up order, and falsifies any universal strict-gain rule based only on an AIPW optimizer.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 on Bayes--minimax duality for randomized confidence sets.
seed_details.kernel: Give an exact finite assignment-tree primal--dual representation of unrestricted honest interval length and use it to certify strict NCC gain.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a dominated fixed experiment with schedule-indexed adaptive record probabilities and reduce interval actions to target-value endpoint hulls.
seed_details.destination_search: Confidence-set duality exists for fixed dominated experiments, but no adaptive platform schedule program with concurrent-record coarsening was located.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine finite linear-program transcription of coverage constraints.
seed_details.rebuttal: The transcription is useful as a certificate but lacks a continuous reduction, so it is retained only as a supporting route and not as the selected kernel.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Theorems on exact and asymptotic design-based confidence sequences and their discussion of dependence on the minimum propensity.
seed_details.kernel: Determine whether an anytime-valid analogue of the coverage-floor phase exists for minimax expected confidence-sequence width under bounded finite-population bandit outcomes.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace fixed-horizon global miscoverage spending by a time-uniform error-spending or e-process constraint and derive the corresponding missing-mass boundary.
seed_details.destination_search: Existing design-based and semiparametric confidence sequences give constructive widths, not unrestricted minimax expected-width phase transitions.
seed_details.red_team: The answer is obtained by substituting an anytime-valid boundary for \(\alpha\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Time-uniform coverage couples all horizons, so no scalar substitution is valid without a new sequential minimax duality argument.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected seed sits between four literatures. Hadad et al. (2021, Theorem 1 and Discussion) and Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024, Theorems 1--3) stabilize AIPW inference under adaptive assignment but do not benchmark width against every honest interval kernel. Ham et al. (2023, Theorem 1) and Li and Zhao (2026, Theorem 4) supply finite-population design-based martingale inference under adaptive assignment, but their targets are validity and limit theory rather than minimax expected length. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Theorem 1 and Corollary 1) characterize minimax expected measure through test inversion and Bayes--minimax duality in fixed dominated experiments; Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, Theorems 3.1--3.2) optimize bias-aware Gaussian intervals over convex classes. Chen and Andrews (2026 version, Theorem 1) derive optimal conditional inference in batched Gaussian adaptive experiments, which differs from unconditional finite-population honesty. Santacatterina et al. (2025, Theorem 3) compare efficient influence functions for concurrent-only and pooled controls, but not unrestricted variable-length kernels. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) optimize finite-population point-estimation risk rather than confidence length. Searches of these target--method pairs found no theorem with the exact \(p_{\mathrm{floor}}=\alpha\) boundary or the displayed all-kernel comparison.
